items.title: Grep for silent except-swallow blocks that might hide another load-bearing bug
items.notes: The plugin_watcher.py hot-reload bug (handoff #13) was invisible for as long as this code existed because a bare AttributeError from a missing reload() method was caught and just logged. Worth a dedicated pass over 'except Exception: pass' / 'except Exception as e: log...' blocks across the codebase specifically looking for ones swallowing something load-bearing rather than genuinely optional, the way this whole audit series (handoffs #6, #9-#14) kept finding real bugs by actually reading and exercising code rather than skimming for style issues.

items.title: Decide fate of the vestigial session_memory param across actions/
items.notes: ~16 action functions accept session_memory=None in their signature (weather_report.py, open_app.py, reminder.py, code_helper.py, dev_agent.py, browser_control.py, send_message.py, computer_settings.py, file_controller.py, screen_processor.py, web_search.py, desktop.py, youtube_video.py, computer_control.py...) but no SessionMemory-like class exists anywhere and every call site passes None or omits it -- confirmed via grep. weather_report.py's 'session_memory.set_last_search(...)' (guarded by 'if session_memory:') is dead code as a result, not an active bug like the plugin_watcher/config_cache ones -- it never fires. Either implement the intended feature or strip the dead parameter across all ~16 signatures.

items.title: Headless server mode (AETHER_HEADLESS=1) + dual-host LLM fallback
items.notes: core/headless_ui.py drop-in for ui.AetherUI with no PyQt6 dependency; main.py gates the PyQt6 bootstrap/import and defensively wraps the sounddevice import on AETHER_HEADLESS=1. core/llm_client.get_llm_settings() gained dual-host resolution -- prefers llm_remote_url (e.g. a home PC's GPU-backed Ollama) when reachable (cached health-check, default 20s interval / 2.5s timeout), falls back to llm_local_url (CPU on this machine) otherwise; unchanged behavior with no llm_remote_url configured. Verified via 9 tests + full suite.

items.title: Remote-approval flow for headless confirm_blocking() + dashboard LLM backend status
items.notes: core/pending_approvals.py (thread-safe ApprovalStore, event-based blocking, fails closed on timeout) + core/notify.py (ntfy push -- new integration, no ntfy setup existed in this codebase before; ntfy_base_url/ntfy_topic added as new config keys). confirm_blocking() registers a pending approval, fires the push, and blocks until dashboard/server.py's new POST /api/approvals/{id}/approve|deny resolves it or times out. AETHER_HEADLESS_AUTO_CONFIRM=1 bypass unchanged. Dashboard also gained GET /api/llm-status surfacing core.llm_client.get_llm_backend_status() (active backend + real IP/host, including the fallback IP), polled in app.html. Verified via 9 tests + full suite; caught and fixed an old test that started blocking for the real 120s default timeout once confirm_blocking() became a genuine blocking call.

items.title: Pending approvals don't survive a restart
items.notes: core/pending_approvals.ApprovalStore is in-memory only. A dashboard/process restart while something's mid-approval loses it -- the calling thread just times out and denies (safe default, not a security hole), but the operator gets no indication the original request ever existed. Worth deciding whether that's acceptable long-term or if approvals should persist (e.g. to disk/sqlite) across restarts.

items.title: ntfy push for approvals is one-shot, no retry/queue
items.notes: core/notify.send_ntfy() is fire-and-forget -- if the push fails (network blip, ntfy down), the approval still shows up in the dashboard's Pending Approvals list, but the operator isn't proactively re-notified and may not know to check. Consider a retry with backoff, or re-pushing once if unresolved after N seconds.

items.title: dashboard/server.py has no standalone entrypoint
items.notes: Noted since the original headless-mode work: start_dashboard_server() only ever gets called from AetherLocal._init_dashboard_and_integrations(), itself only reachable after the full AetherLocal boot sequence runs. Fine for the current headless design (still boots AetherLocal, just skips the GUI), but if a lighter API-only deployment (dashboard + approvals + LLM status, nothing else) is ever wanted, this coupling needs breaking.

items.title: Client-side parser for raw <tool_call> text from Ollama (needs user approval)

items.title: actions/desktop.py exec() sandbox is escapable and runs model-written code without a confirmation
items.notes: safe_builtins exposes getattr and the sandbox passes Path/time objects, so getattr(Path.__init__,'__globals__') reaches os/sys; Windows also exposes ctypes. Needs a design decision: confirmation via core/safety, or a real allowlist DSL instead of exec. See handoff #39.

items.title: Dashboard: replace AES-CBC (no MAC, key = SHA-256 of the 6-char session code) with AES-GCM and a random per-session key
items.notes: dashboard/server.py _aes_key/decrypt: anyone who captures one ciphertext can brute-force the ~30-bit code offline in seconds, and CBC without a MAC is malleable. Needs a matching change in the CryptoJS client in dashboard/static, so it must be tested with a real phone/browser. Over plain HTTP (no config/certs) the traffic is also sniffable.
